---
title: "Course Content"
---

Welcome to the course content area of the SciLifeLab Training Webpage Template.

This section contains example pages that demonstrate how you can structure and format the learning materials for your own course. Use them as a starting point when creating your content.  
     
     
## Explore the examples

The modules in the navigation demonstrate different content elements and ways of presenting information.

- **Module 1 – Structuring a page:** Learn how to use headings, paragraphs, lists, and other basic text formatting.
- **Module 2 – Highlighting information:** Explore callout boxes that can be used for tips, notes, warnings, and important information.
- **Module 3 – Adding media and interactive elements:** See examples of links, images, embedded videos, and other content elements.

Some pages also include example exercises, tables, code blocks, and reflection questions.

## How to use these examples

Each page contains rendered examples and the corresponding Markdown or Quarto syntax.

1. Browse the examples using the module navigation above.
2. Find an element you would like to use in your course.
3. Copy the corresponding code snippet from the example page.
4. Paste it into your own `.qmd` file and replace the placeholder text with your content.
5. Render your website to check how the content looks.

You do not need to use every example. Choose the elements that suit your course and remove the ones you do not need.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Tip

You can combine different elements on the same page. For example, a topic might start with learning objectives, introduce a concept using headings and paragraphs, highlight a key idea in a callout box, and finish with a reflection question.
:::

## Creating your own course content

The examples in this section are intended to be adapted. Replace the demonstration text with your own material, and add or remove pages to match the structure of your course.

For instructions on organising your content files and configuring the course modules, see the template user guide.

Happy authoring!
